The most likely corrupted element is **M3**. Its width (43.94 µm, about 6.6× M4's 6.635 µm at the same L = 0.153 µm) pushes it into weak inversion (Vgs = 0.694 V < Vth = 0.785 V). A reference cascode sized that way shifts the bias node operating points, which lowers rout. The current and compliance specs still pass because the mirror ratio and the R1-set reference current are intact.

M1 ranks second because it has the largest rout sensitivity (+22.4%). Its W and L match M2's, though, so it is less likely to be the fault. M4 ranks third because its rout sensitivity is small.
